scenarios: Release 1 (09_ §2). The Release-2 call-review and email-triage scenarios are parked, not deleted — see 09_ §1.
status: NOT BUILT — no Zapier account exists in the Builder environment

every_http_step_must_send.X-Provider-Key: the provider credential the stub prints at startup (no owner authority; distinct from the owner key)
every_http_step_must_send.Content-Type: application/json — the stub refuses anything else (SEC-R1-08)

zaps.name: Builder-return pipeline

steps.config: Builder return artifact (zip + manifest)

Apply the envelope AND bind the five-component identity tuple: task_id, transition, artifact_digest (COMPUTED here from the artifact, never taken from the sender), target_role (symbolic), submission_epoch. Carry the owner-minted registration_ref through unchanged; if the submission has none, stop here and record the refusal — this step cannot mint one.
steps.boundary: 25_ A.1 — a raw archive hash alone is not identity. 25_ A.2 — the artifact identity is owner-registered at /owner/artifact/register; the digest computed here is only ever CHECKED AGAINST it and is never an authority on its own.

steps.config: AI OS /poc1/review-case with registration_ref plus the five identity components and the external-untrusted envelope
steps.boundary: returns a resume token, OR duplicate-suppressed with the prior receipt and reprocessed:false, OR one of three distinguishable rejections: rejected-artifact-binding (403, the submission disagrees with the owner registration), rejected-unauthorized-target (403), rejected-unknown-target (400)

steps.config: outcome equals case-opened
steps.boundary: duplicate suppression and target rejection must NOT read as success

steps.app: Human in the Loop by Zapier
steps.config: Carries the pause only. The card and the decision live on the AI OS surface; Zapier never learns the case id
steps.boundary: packet §3 — the provider may carry the pause, never decide it

steps.config: AI OS /poc1/verify-decision with ONLY {token}
steps.boundary: the endpoint is an allowlist; any additional field is refused

steps.config: authorized is true
POST to action_request.endpoint with {capability, action_request_id, case_id, payload} exactly as returned — the payload is the one the AI OS authorized, not one this Zap composes
steps.boundary: 25_ A.4 — the destination comes from the ActionRequest the AI OS built by resolving the ROLE, and the capability binds the idempotency identity, action request, case, endpoint and canonical payload digest. A replay of the SAME payload returns the prior receipt with no_second_side_effect:true; a DIFFERENT payload from a delivered state is refused, as is any delivery on REVOKED, EXPIRED or UNCERTAIN.

steps.config: AI OS /poc1/receipt with {action_request_id, case_id, provider_status in {ok,error,uncertain}, provider_message, destination_digest_claimed (or null), provider_metrics}
steps.boundary: 25_ A.6 — CORROBORATING ONLY. This step cannot mark an action delivered, alter capability state or satisfy any acceptance check, and a provider_status of 'ok' is a provider claim rather than a service conclusion. A receipt arriving after the capability is REVOKED or EXPIRED is captured, refused, and changes nothing.

steps.config: On an ambiguous or timed-out relay: AI OS /poc1/reconcile with {capability, action_request_id}
steps.boundary: 25_ A.5 — this route returns RECONCILED_DELIVERED or UNCERTAIN and can NEVER return RECONCILED_NOT_DELIVERED. Local absence is not proof: only an owner attestation on /owner/reconcile reaches not-delivered, and exactly one re-attempt is permitted after it. Do not retry from UNCERTAIN — the wrapper refuses it.

measures: unauthorized-target rejection distinguishable from duplicate success
uncertain-result reconciliation outcome, and whether the fabric offered any way to distinguish delivered from not-delivered without the owner
r1p05_artifact_measures: binary fidelity and digest preservation end to end
behaviour on nested archives, symlinks, traversal paths and malformed archives (failing closed is a recordable capability gap, not a POC failure)
whether the provider stores, inspects or retains artifact contents
owner-card latency without the artifact entering Discord

zaps.name: Idea capture and staging

steps.config: Idea intake, Business partition only

Bind the request: carry the owner-minted idea_ref (Case A) or, with no ref, send the top-level external-untrusted envelope (Case B). Give EVERY external item its own envelope. Any owner_content sent is a convenience copy only.
steps.boundary: 25_ A.3 — authority derives ONLY from an idea_ref the owner minted at /owner/idea against content the wrapper stored server-side. A convenience copy that does not canonicalize to the stored owner_content_digest is refused 403; owner_content without a valid idea_ref is refused 403 and is never owner-authored. An item never inherits authority from the enclosing idea, and any origin/trust/instruction_authority this Zap sets is ignored for authority and recorded as provider-supplied.

steps.config: AI OS /poc2/triage — new-topic vs existing-project-addition, staged record, and the instruction-authority verdict
steps.boundary: the AI OS classifies; Zapier transports

steps.config: instruction_authority is 'none' whenever origin is 'external'
steps.boundary: the POC's proof obligation: external content informs classification WITHOUT acquiring instruction authority

explicitly_absent: no send step of any kind
measures: trust isolation across the two cases
zaps.assertion: Read authority_components from the response and confirm every external_items[i] carries instruction_authority 'none'. A single flattened authority value for the whole request is a defect (25_ A.3), so an assertion written against one top-level field does not satisfy this.

zaps.name: Durable nightly integrity sweep

steps.config: 03:00 local
steps.boundary: the provider hosts the schedule; the AI OS journal owns the spec

steps.config: AI OS /poc3/run-started declaring schedule_id and occurrence, and passing the Zap run id as provider_correlation_id
steps.boundary: 25_ §B — run identity is STUB-MINTED; this Zap never chooses a run_id, and any provider correlation value is carried separately and anchors nothing. A duplicate declaration of the same (schedule_id, occurrence) is a 409 that PRESERVES the prior started_at and checkpoint count — a duplicate run-started is itself a POC-3 measurement, never an overwrite. After the induced kill, expect that 409 and continue against the run_id it returns.

steps.config: POST to the returned stage_endpoint with {run_id}; leave Zapier's autoreplay/retry enabled
steps.boundary: 25_ §B — /stage/deliver is RETRY-TOLERANT by design: the round induces a mid-flight kill, and a single-use rule here would mis-score the provider retry POC-3 exists to measure.

steps.config: AI OS /poc3/checkpoint
side_effect_certain is true; otherwise branch to /poc3/reconcile
steps.boundary: 25_ §B — the wrapper compares only what it recorded and reports external_post_state_checked:false. It never asserts a check it did not perform; record that as the answer, not as a gap in the run.

steps.config: AI OS /poc3/receipt

zaps.induced_failure_required: kill the run mid-flight between the stage and the checkpoint and record the ACTUAL retry/replay behaviour — packet §4 forbids simulating this in prose. The stub's 409-on-duplicate-declaration preserves the prior run record so 'resumed' and 'replayed from the top' are distinguishable, which they were not in R1
measures: stage attempts recorded separately from deliveries

contract: 25_ Revision 5 (§A/§B). The route policy is the authority: a field a route does not list is reduced to a descriptor under the provider provenance key and never reaches the top level of a capture.
